key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN surrogate model can accurately predict friction stir welding behavior in HDPE and identify process windows that avoid weld defects.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers choose rotational speed, welding speed, and preheating settings to improve joint quality, reduce force spikes, and prevent wormholes in thermoplastic welding.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE friction stir welding
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force data
Process map generation across rotational speed, travel speed, and bottom preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong prediction accuracy with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental thermal, force, and defect observations.
watch_item: The surrogate model is trained on a limited experimental parameter space, so performance may drop when extrapolating to new tool designs, materials, or welding conditions.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
